8539.t: CE6619: Design and Construction of Underground Structures
8539.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6619 : Design and Construction of Underground Structures { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module I: Introduction to Rock Engineering Basics (6 hours)
Rocks and rock masses, Physical and mechanical properties, classification and failure criteria, Underground excavations, Ground conditions, Planning and exploration for various underground construction projects, Stereographic projection method, Principle and application in underground excavation design.
Module II: Stress distribution of tunnels (8 hours)
In-situ stress, Elastic stress distribution around tunnels, Stress distribution for different shapes and under different in-situ stress conditions, Greenspan method, design principles, multiple openings, openings in laminated rocks, elasto-plastic analysis of tunnels.
Module III: Analysis of underground openings (8 hours)
Application of rock mass classification systems, Ground conditions in tunneling, Analysis of underground openings in squeezing and swelling ground, Empirical methods, Estimation of elastic modulus and modulus of deformation of rocks, Uniaxial jacking /plate jacking tests, Radial jacking and Goodman jacking tests, Long term behavior of tunnels and caverns, New Austrian tunneling Method (NATM), Norwegian Tunnelling Method (NMT).
Module IV: Design of support systems (8 hours)
Rock mass-tunnel support interaction analysis, Ground response, Support reaction curves, Ladanyi's elasto-plastic analysis of tunnels, Design of various support systems including concrete and shotcrete linings, steel sets, rock bolting, and rock anchoring, Combined support systems, Estimation of the load-carrying capacity of rock bolts, permeability, and grouting.
Module V: Instrumentation and monitoring of underground excavations (6 hours)
In-situ stress, flat jack, hydraulic fracturing, single and multi-point borehole extensometers, load cells, pressure cells, During and after construction, various case studies.

Course Objective

1 .

To impart knowledge regarding the basics of rock engineering, including rock properties, classification, and underground excavation design.
2 .

To impart knowledge regarding analyzing stress distribution around tunnels using elastic and elastoplastic methods and design principles.
3 .

To impart knowledge regarding evaluation of underground openings through rock mass classification and empirical methods, considering long-term behavior.
4 .

To impart knowledge regarding the design and analysis of support systems for tunnels, including concrete linings, rock bolting, and combined support systems.

Course Outcome

1 .

CO1: The students will be able to understand the need and importance of underground space technology.
CO2: The students will be able to understand the hazards of underground excavations and environmental problems.
CO3: The students will be able to understand the applicability of various types of underground excavating machines and drilling patterns.
CO4: The students can select and design the underground support for different mining conditions.
CO5: The students will be able to understand the instrumentation and monitoring of underground excavations.

Essential Reading

1 .

R.E. Goodman, Introduction to Rock Mechanics, John Wiley & Sons

2 .

E. Hoek, and E.T. Brown, Underground Excavations, Spon Press

Supplementary Reading

1 .

L. Obert, and W.I. Duvall, Rock Mechanics and Design of Structures in Rocks, John Wiley

2 .

B. Singh, and R.K. Goel, Tunneling in Weak Rocks, Elsevier

7771.t: BM6033: Intellectual Property Right and Bio-safety for Bioengineers
7771.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM6033 : Intellectual Property Right and Bio-safety for Bioengineers { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module: 1 Introduction to IPR and its historical background, National IPR Policy, Types of IPR - terms and terminologies, their evolution through amendments and current status ( 8 lectures)
Module: 2 Structure of patent, Patent searching and search tools Patent drafting – Specification and Claims Patent application process, PCT process and filing procedure, Managing Legal Issues of the Patenting Process Enforcement copyright laws and its importance, Trademarks: its importance and applications, trade secrets, Industrial designs, Protection of new varieties of plants, Geographical Indications and Integrated Circuits, Important Cases and Discussions. (12 Lectures)
Module: 3 Introduction to bio-safety Terminologies, Types of containments, Elements of containments, Bio-safety levels, Biosafety categories shipping and transport of regulated biological materials Mechanism of implementing biosafety Containment facilities and biosafety practices: Code of practice Laboratory design and facilities Laboratory equipment Health and medical surveillance Emergency procedures Decontamination and disposal Recombinant safety considerations Risk assessment, Biosafety for GM foods, medical devices, agricultural practices and others (10 lectures)
Module: 4 Bioethics: principles, role of ethics in biotech and biomedical research and innovations, case studies related to ethics of modern advances in biotechnology and biomedical sciences (8 lectures)

Course Objective

1 .

• To gain an understanding of IPR drafting, filing and protection
2 .

• To understand bio-safety in biotechnology and biomedical engineering.
3 .

• To familiarize with the national guidelines on bio-safety.
4 .

• To understand the relevance of ethical practices in biotechnology and biomedical research and Innovations

Course Outcome

1 .

• Understand the basics of IPR, procedure of filing, prosecution and protection.
• Learn the national IPR policies especially those related to biotechnology and medical engineering.
• Understand bio-safety issues in biotechnology and medical engineering.
• Learn governmental rules and regulations with respect to bio-safety.
• Understand bio-ethical issues in biotechnology and medical engineering.

Essential Reading

1 .

Government of India, The Indian Patent Act. 1970, Government of India , Intellectual property rights: law and practice, The institute of company secretaries of India, July, 2015

2 .

DBT and BCIL., Guidelines and Handbook for Institutional Biosafety, DBT and BCIL. , Goel And Parashar, IPR, Biosafety and Bioethics, Pearson 1st edition (1 January 2013)

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Narayanan, P, Patent Law, Eastern Law House, India

2 .

World Health Organization, WHO Biosafety Manual, World Health Organization

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CR6431 : Glass Science { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Thermodynamics of Glass:
TTT diagram for glass. Glass Transition Range behaviour. Viscosity and viscoelastic properties. Relaxation behaviour of glass.
Module 2: Electrochemical Behaviour of Glass
Redox and Electrochemical behavior, Optical Basicity, Colouration, Finning mechanism
Module 3: Structure Property Correlation in Glass:
Transport Phenomena, Surface Tension, Density, . Phase Separation. Durability of glass.
Module 4 : Thermal Porpertuies of glass
Heat Capacity, Thermal analysis of glass Thermal Expansion Annealing and Strengthening and tempering: Mechanism and Process. Surface treatment.
Module: 5 Mechanical Properties of Glass.
Brittle nature of glass, glasses for the strategic Sector for mechanical applications
Module 6: Optical Properties of glass:
Refraction, Laser Glass, Linear and non linear optical properties, Solar glass
Electrical and dielectric properties of glass. Modern application of glass.

Course Objective

1 .

To enable participants to relate the chemical composition and atomic-level structure of glass to its observable physical and chemical properties.
2 .

To study crucial material properties such as mechanical strength, thermal insulation, viscosity, and optical characteristics, and how to measure or predict them.
3 .

To understand the fundamental science behind how glass forms, including the cooling rate effects and the glassy state
4 .

Focusing on emission reduction, energy efficiency, and sustainable production techniques.

Course Outcome

1 .

An ability to identify, formulate, and solve complex engineering problems by applying principles of engineering, science, and mathematics
2 .

An ability to describe the fundamentals of the atomic structure of glass.
3 .

An ability to explain the properties (e.g. physical, thermal, mechanical , optical etc) of glasses and relate the properties to the atomic structure
4 .

Select and recommend a glass for specific technical/engineering applications

7003.t: CY3106: Purifications and Characterizations of Organic Compounds
7003.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CY3106 : Purifications and Characterizations of Organic Compounds { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Chromatography: Adsorption chromatography, Partition chromatography, Paper chromatography, Thin-layer chromatography, column chromatography, gas-liquid chromatography, ion-exchange chromatography.
Spectroscopic techniques of characterization: UV-Vis spectroscopy (Basic principle, instrumentation, characteristic absorptions of organic compounds, IR Spectroscopy (Basic principle, instrumentation, modes of vibration, absorption trends, analysis of IR sprctrum), NMR Spectroscopy (1H NMR, Basic principle, chemical shift and shielding, instrumentation, chemical equivalence, magnetic equivalence, spin-spin coupling, NMR spectrum of simple organic compounds), Mass-spectrometry (Basic Principle, instrumentation, ionization methods, fragementation, molecular ion peak, metastable peak, McLafferty rearrangement, nitrogen rule, Mass analysis of simple compounds). Comprehensive problems on structure elucidation of small organic molecules.

Course Objective

1 .

To learn the basic principles of techniques used for purification and characterizations of organic compounds.
2 .

To learn how to make structural assignments and characterization of organic compounds using various spectroscopic technologies, especially Mass, UV-Vis, IR, and 1H-NMR techniques

Course Outcome

1 .

CO 1: It provides the knowledge of different separation method of organic compounds including chromatography, distillation, sublimation, crystallisation and filtration techniques.
CO 2: It provides the knowledge of different chromatographic method of separation and their applications.
CO 3: It enables the students to learn the basic characterization of organic compounds using UV-vis, IR spectroscopy methods.
CO 4: It provides knowledge of basic principles, instrumentation of NMR spectroscopy and how to characterize the organic molecules using this spectroscopic method.
CO 5: It provides knowledge of basic principles, instrumentation of Mass-spectrometry and their application in synthetic research.
CO 6: In addition, at the end of the session, it enables the students to learn single crystal X-ray diffraction methodology for analyzing the structure of single crystal of any compound.

Essential Reading

1 .

D. C. Pavia, G. M. Lampman, G. S. Kriz, Introduction to Spectroscopy, THOMSON , 3rd Edition, 2007

2 .

R. K. Bansal, A text book of Organic Chemistry, New Age International Publisher , 5th Edition, 2007

Supplementary Reading

1 .

B. H. Williams, I. Flemming, Spectroscopy Methods in Organic Chemistry, McGraw Hill , 2005

2 .

Bessler and Silverstein, Spectroscopy of Organic Compounds, JOHN WILEY , 2001

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CY5701 : Environmental Chemistry { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

1. Estimation of halides in water samples by potentiometric titration.
2. Determination of pH, salinity, and conductivity of water samples. Measurement of water quality parameters: Colour, turbidity, temperature, acidity and alkalinity.
3. Estimation of Co2+ and Ni2+ by colorimetry/ spectrophotometry.
4. Estimation of alkali metals (Na +, K+) in various samples by flame-photometry.
5. Determination of heavy metals including mercury, Arsenic by AAS.
6. Spectrophotometric Methods of Estimation: Fluoride, Nitrate, Phosphate, Chromate [Cr6+], sulphates.
7. Spectrophotometric Methods of Estimation Hg, Pb, Cd.
8. Spectrophotometric Methods of Estimation of one pesticide, phenol, Estimation of C, N, S in coal and soil samples by CHNS Instrument.
9. Estimation of a) Cyanide, b) Detergents (colorimetric method) c) Oil and grease in water.
10. Preparation of simple coagulant and stabilizer for water treatment. Estimation of TDS by turbidometry.

Course Objective

1 .

1. To impart hands on experience in performing qualitative as well as quantitative detection of environmental harmful chemical compounds and ions.
2 .

2. To elucidate the use of different simple instrumental techniques for sensing of harmful chemical substances and ions.

Course Outcome

1 .

1. To learn and understand the chemical methods of quantitative detection of environmental harmful chemicals.
2 .

2. To learn how to perform calorimetric and other experimental techniques for evaluate environmental harmful substances.

3 .

3. To learn simple instrumental techniques used in chemical analysis.

Essential Reading

1 .

R Gopalan, A Laboratory Manual For Environmental Chemistry, I K International publishing , Describes 72 experiments that analyse soil, water and air samples.

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Ruth Ann Murphy, Environmental Chemistry in the Lab, CRC press , a comprehensive approach to modern environmental chemistry laboratory instruction, together with a complete experimental experience.

Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : PH2073 : Properties of Matter Laboratory { 0-0-3 / 2}

Subject Nature : Practical

Syllabus

Module 1 :

1. Determination of acceleration due to gravity ‘g’ by Kater’s Pendulum.
2. Determination of spring constant and effective mass of a given spiral spring.
3. Verification of the laws of transverse vibration using Sonomter.
4. Determination of the moment of inertia and radius of gyration using bifilar suspension.
5. Determination of the moment of inertia of fly wheel.
6. Determination of Poission’s ratio of the rubber.
7. Determination of the rigidity of modulus using Torsional pendulum.
8. Determination of the rigidity of modulus using Searle’s static apparatus.
9. Determination of the rigidity of modulus of copper wire using statical method.
10. Determination of the Young’s modulus by cantilever bending method.
11. Determination of the Young’s modulus of a given beam by bending using travelling microscope.
12. Determination of the rigidity of modulus of cooper wire using Maxwell’s needle.

Course Objective

1 .

Measurement of acceleration due to gravity ‘g’ by Kater’s Pendulum.
2 .

Measurement of moment of inertia of solid.
3 .

Measurement of spring constant and effective mass of a given spiral spring.
4 .

Verification of the laws of transverse vibration using Sonomter.
5. Determination of the rigidity of modulus and Young's modulus of different physical systems.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, students will be able to:
CO1: Perform effectively experiments on the measurement of acceleration due to gravity ‘g’ by Kater’s Pendulum.
CO2: Perform effectively experiment on the measurement rigidity of modulus and Young's modulus of different physical systems.
CO3: Verify the laws of transverse vibration using Sonomter.
CO4: Determine the moment of inertia of the bifilar suspension and flywheel.
CO5: Measure the spring constant and effective mass of a given spiral spring.
